summary.intent: Execute issue #644's five pre-`crates/fuse` hardware verification gates for the FUSE-T driver decision — measure invalidation/coherence behavior, replay v1 flake scenarios, check rename atomicity, research licensing, and (if possible) spike FSKit — then land the results and open a reviewed PR.
summary.outcome: Gates 1-4 were run and documented (noattrcache required for coherence, cross-client flake fixed, rename atomicity holds, license needs commercial negotiation); results and blueprint updates were committed and pushed as draft PR #736, passed /simplify (5 fixes applied) and /security-review (clean); gate 5 (FSKit) remains blocked pending a macOS 27 beta VM the user was still trying to provision.

repo: blueprint/desktop.md and blueprint/testing.md are the normative source of truth; measurement provenance and dated run-status belong in tools/*/RESULTS.md, not the blueprint itself
tools/hw-gates is intentionally a standalone crate outside the frozen root Cargo.lock/workspace to avoid moving product dependencies
The vendored fuser fork (with FUSE-T socket-read fragmentation patch) lives on the frozen 'v1' branch, not in the current tree's vendor dir (which was just a stale Cargo.lock)
FUSE-T and macFUSE both register as 'fuse' in pkg-config, so an unconstrained build can silently link macFUSE and trigger its kext approval prompt — must pin to fuse-t.pc / verify with otool -L
Bare '#47' style issue references in blueprint/desktop.md are an existing repo convention referring to FSM1/cipher-box-next issues, not the current repo
commit messages in this repo follow commitlint format with 'Refs #NNN' trailers

code.finding: Patched to prefer fuse-t.pc over macfuse-4-compat during pkg-config probing so builds link libfuse-t.dylib instead of macFUSE
New build script emits the rpath via cargo:rustc-link-arg using the pkg-config-probed fuse-t libdir, replacing a hardcoded global rustflag in .cargo/config.toml (altitude fix from /simplify)
child_for_rename has a unique-prefix rename fallback that was silently masking gate 3's own truncation-bug detection; changed to fail the gate on any fallback hit instead of just counting it
Product-side FUSE crate is still just a 20-line placeholder ('the real FS projection lands in later PRs') — no Filesystem impl or fuser dep yet

workflow: /simplify's 4-angle parallel review (reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude) surfaced concrete duplication (store-mutation boilerplate x9, read_first x2, measurement-loop scaffold x9) and one real altitude issue (hardcoded rpath) even on a throwaway measurement harness
/security-review's sub-agent identification + parallel false-positive-filtering pipeline returned zero findings when the diff was legitimately clean, rather than manufacturing noise
Background bash tasks for long-running measurement gates (10s-300s deadlines) surface via task-notification and can be picked up later without polling

After the kext dialog, the assistant continued working through several more tool calls instead of immediately answering the user's confused message, and did so twice in a row, causing real user frustration ('the actual fuck' / 'my messages were ignored twice in a row')
